prediction.likelyOutcome: This is a hard-fought jury valuation case in which neither side's number should be taken at face value: Osher's valuation is compromised by its reliance on a tax-credit-tainted 2011 sale, while LCRA's is compromised by post-taking condition evidence and a refusal to weigh historic designation. Expect a verdict in the broad middle of the presented range, likely closer to the owner's appraiser's figure than LCRA's, net of the commissioners' deposit already paid, with a real possibility that the excluded qualification/comparable-development photographic evidence becomes grounds for post-verdict relief if the verdict comes in low.

issues.label: Just Compensation — Fair Market Value at Date of Taking

figures.label: Spence appraisal (owner's appraiser)
figures.quote: Spence testified the fair market value of the Property at the time of the taking was $4.93 million.

figures.label: Neff appraisal (LCRA's appraiser)
figures.quote: LCRA called John Neff, its appraiser, who testified the fair market value of the Property at the time of the taking was $573,000

figures.label: Commissioners' award deposited and received by owner
figures.quote: the commissioners awarded $817,589.59. LCRA deposited the award, with interest, in the circuit court and took title to the Property.

issues.label: Reliability of the 2011 Sale as Comparable Valuation Evidence
Reliability of LCRA's Post-Taking Condition Evidence
Exclusion of Owner's Qualification/Comparable-Development Photographic Evidence

outcome.description: After a seven-day jury trial in May 2018 the jury awarded $573,000, the value given by LCRA's appraiser and $244,589.59 below the commissioners' $817,589.59 award (the owner's appraiser said $4.93 million); the court denied a post-trial homestead allowance and taxed $21,207.13 costs against the owner. The Eastern District affirmed on April 21, 2020.

source.caseName: Land Clearance for Redevelopment Authority of the City of St. Louis v. James Townsend Osher
source.court: Missouri Court of Appeals, Eastern District, Division Two, on appeal from the Circuit Court of the City of St. Louis
source.excerptNote: Verbatim from the Factual and Procedural Background: Pre-Trial (condemnation filing, commissioners' award, exceptions) and Trial (each side's evidence, including both appraisers). Removed: the Introduction (judgment amount and costs), the judge-assignment/recusal motions, footnotes 1-4 and one footnote marker, the 'Jury Verdict and Homestead Allowance' section and everything after it. LCRA's appraiser's figure, which the jury adopted, is retained as a party's stated position, so amountIsTheRequestedAmount is true. The building was zoned industrial; the owner's post-verdict homestead (primary-residence) claim was denied and is not part of the input.
